title: 'Never seen anything quite like it': How rural Pennsylvania's $165 million data center fight became representative of the bipartisan battle against AI
key_facts: NorthPoint Development offered Hazle Township's 4,500 residents a potential $10,000 each in exchange for permission to build a 1,300-acre data centre, part of a $165 million proposed investment (Project Hazelnut).

About 30 properties in nearby Sugarloaf Township faced eminent domain threats over a proposed high-voltage power line to serve the data centre; locals formed Alliance to Stop the Line and filed 20 formal protests.
Emails cited by Fortune name Amazon as the end user; an Amazon spokesperson said it is evaluating multiple sites across the Commonwealth and has no definitive agreement with NorthPoint.
About 70 percent of Americans oppose local data centre construction in one Gallup poll (75 percent of Democrats, 63 percent of Republicans).

At least 75 data centre projects worth over $130 billion were delayed or cancelled in the first three months of 2026, and active opposition groups grew from 396 to 833, per a Data Center Watch report published in June.

Governor Josh Shapiro signed an executive order in August eliminating fast-track permits and gave local agencies power to approve data centre projects; Pennsylvania's election for governor is next month.
Texas Governor Greg Abbott moved from calling Texas the epicentre of AI development to restrictions and halting pending approvals on 1,800 proposals, according to a University of Michigan professor.
quote_evidence: An Amazon spokesperson told Fortune it is “evaluating multiple sites across the Commonwealth” but does not have a definitive agreement in place with NorthPoint.
About 70% of Americans oppose data center construction in their local areas, according to one Gallup poll, including 75% of Democrats and 63% of Republicans.
why_it_matters_hint: A local fight in Pennsylvania shows data centre opposition crossing party lines in an election year.
notes: Feature article; the poll and project counts are third-party figures quoted by Fortune. Amazon disputes that it has a definitive agreement.
